{
  "research_question": "Does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success' (binary 0/1), explicitly note that ANOVA is suboptimal; consider a Chi-square test of independence or logistic regression as a primary alternative, but proceed with ANOVA only if normality can be approximated via large sample size (n=76655).",
    "For 'Path Efficiency' and 'AD', check for skewness given the min/max ranges (0 to ~29.8 and 0 to 1.0 respectively) and consider log-transformation if residuals are non-normal.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target' and 'Average Speed', verify normality of residuals and homogeneity of variances across the five groups."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that each row represents a unique trial and that trials are not clustered within specific mice in a way that violates independence (random effects model may be needed if mouse ID is a blocking factor).",
    "Normality of residuals: Inspect Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of each ANOVA model.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Conduct Levene's test or Bartlett's test to ensure variance is equal across the five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Outlier detection: Identify extreme values in 'Time-to-Target' (max 201.39) and 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.82) that could unduly influence the F-statistic.",
    "For 'Success': Assess the distribution of successes/failures per group; if any group has <5 successes or failures, Fisher's Exact Test is required instead of ANOVA."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus F-test is significant for any variable, conduct Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test to perform pairwise comparisons between all five stimulation paradigms while controlling the family-wise error rate.",
    "If sample sizes are unequal (which they are: Combined=48846 vs Sham=3505), ensure the post-hoc test uses the appropriate adjustment for unbalanced designs (Tukey-Kramer).",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared or Cohen's d) for significant pairwise differences to quantify the magnitude of the paradigm effect."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed) compared to 'Sham' and single-modality conditions.",
    "Significant differences are expected between 'ICMS Only' and 'Dim Visual Only' vs 'Bright Visual Only' depending on the specific sensory integration hypothesis of the experiment.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in the 'Combined' condition and highest in the 'Sham' condition, indicating better path straightness with multimodal stimulation.",
    "Due to the massive imbalance in sample sizes (Combined has ~64% of data), the statistical power to detect differences involving 'Combined' will be very high, while power for comparisons involving 'Sham' or 'Bright Visual Only' may be lower."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes across stimulation paradigms (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) may inflate Type I error rates or reduce power for underrepresented groups.",
    "Potential violation of independence if multiple trials per mouse are treated as independent data points without accounting for the 'Mouse' random effect (8 levels).",
    "Skewness in 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.8) and 'Time-to-Target' (max 201.4) may violate ANOVA normality assumptions without transformation.",
    "Binary nature of 'Success' makes ANOVA an approximation; a generalized linear model (GLM) with binomial distribution is theoretically more appropriate.",
    "Missingness is reported as 0, but the filtering process removed 2022 rows, potentially introducing selection bias if the removed rows were non-random."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM) for continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) and a Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) with binomial link for 'Success', including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures within subjects, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons with p-value adjustment."
}
